findings.reason: The diff deletes the `node.tag !== defaultScalarTag.tagName` early return, so now only isKey and style are checked. presenter.ts:417 sets shouldPrintTag whenever the style is not PLAIN and the tag is not the default str tag, so non-strings come out quoted and tagged. That goes against the documented 'Quotes all non-key strings' (presenter.ts:99). I kept Codex's high severity because every forceQuotes user gets different output. story.md is not in the packet, so I can't say whether the story asked for this.
findings.claim: With the tag guard removed, forceQuotes now quotes every plain non-key scalar, including ints, floats, booleans and null, not just strings. Because the value is quoted, it also gets an explicit tag, so 42 is written as !!int '42'.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (layout.node.tag !== layout.presenterOptions.schema.defaultScalarTag.tagName) return` and rewrites the comment from 'plain string values' to 'plain values'. Once the style is no longer PLAIN, presenter.ts:417 sets `shouldPrintTag` for any node whose tag isn't the default str tag (`layout.style !== SCALAR_STYLE.PLAIN && node.tag !== state.defaultScalarTagName`), so every non-string value gets an explicit tag plus quotes. The option's docs still say 'Quotes all non-key strings using {@link quoteStyle}' (src/ast/presenter.ts:99), and CHANGELOG.md:134 describes forceQuotes as 'force quoting non-key strings'. The packet's acceptance.md points to a story.md that isn't in the packet or the export, so the intent can't be confirmed.
